No dangerous commands (e.g., `eval`, `curl|bash`, `wget`) are present, and there is no evidence of data exfiltration, remote code execution, or tampering with system files outside the package directory. The license and dependencies are properly declared, and the installation steps place only the expected binary and license file into standard system locations. The source points to a tarball hosted on GitHub at a legitimate upstream URL: https://github.com/zackees/reld. The SHA-256 checksum is provided and matches the expected format, indicating a verifiable source integrity check.

The package description identifies it as a fork of weld, a polylinker supporting incremental linking — a plausible development tool.

No obfuscation, suspicious URLs, or unauthorized network activity is present. All content aligns with standard AUR packaging practices. While the .SRCINFO does not itself enforce security, its contents are benign and do not indicate any malicious intent or supply-chain compromise.
